records.name: Natural Sciences
records.en: The empirical study of the physical universe — matter, energy, life, Earth, and the cosmos — through observation, experiment, and testable theory. Spans physics, chemistry, biology, the Earth sciences, and astronomy; distinguished from the formal sciences by its grounding in evidence and from applied science by its pursuit of explanation rather than use.
records.cs: Empirické zkoumání přírody — hmoty, energie, života, Země i vesmíru — prostřednictvím pozorování, experimentu a ověřitelných teorií. Zahrnuje fyziku, chemii, biologii, vědy o Zemi a astronomii; od formálních věd se liší oporou v empirických důkazech, od aplikovaných věd snahou o vysvětlení, nikoli o využití.
records.brief:
The natural sciences comprise the empirical study of the physical universe — matter, energy, life, planets, and the cosmos — through observation, experiment, and theories that make testable predictions. Their unifying commitment is methodological: claims stand or fall on evidence, instruments extend the senses, and mathematics supplies the language in which laws are stated. From this shared method the natural sciences have produced the most reliable body of knowledge humanity possesses, from the structure of the atom to the age of the universe.

Internally the domain layers by scale and subject. [[01.01]] Physics states the fundamental laws of matter, energy, and force; [[01.02]] Chemistry studies how substances combine and transform; [[01.03]] Biology examines living systems from molecules to ecosystems; [[01.04]] Earth Sciences treat the planet itself — its rocks, oceans, atmosphere, and climate; and [[01.05]] Astronomy extends inquiry beyond Earth to stars, galaxies, and the universe at large. Each level draws on those beneath it: chemistry rests on quantum physics, biology on chemistry, and the Earth and space sciences integrate all of them into planetary and cosmic histories.

The domain's boundaries are drawn by method and aim. The [[02]] Formal Sciences supply the mathematics, logic, and computation the natural sciences use but are not themselves empirical; [[03]] Applied Sciences & Technology turns natural-scientific findings toward practical ends; and the [[04]] Social Sciences apply comparable empirical methods to human behavior and institutions. See [Encyclopaedia Britannica: science](https://www.britannica.com/science/science) and [Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Scientific Method](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/scientific-method/).

records.name: Formal Sciences
records.en: The study of abstract formal systems — number, structure, computation, inference, information, and organized complexity — whose truths are established by definition and proof rather than observation. Encompasses mathematics, computer science, logic, information theory, and systems theory; it supplies the languages and methods the empirical sciences use to model the world.
records.cs: Studium abstraktních formálních systémů — čísel, struktur, výpočtů, úsudku, informace a organizované složitosti — jejichž pravdy se opírají o definice a důkazy, nikoli o pozorování. Zahrnuje matematiku, informatiku, logiku, teorii informace a teorii systémů; poskytuje jazyky a metody, jimiž empirické vědy modelují svět.
records.brief:
The formal sciences study abstract systems of structure and inference — number, computation, proof, information, and organized complexity — whose results are established by definition and demonstration rather than by observation. A theorem, once proved, holds in every possible world that satisfies its axioms; this independence from experiment distinguishes the formal sciences from every empirical domain and makes them the common infrastructure of exact thought.

[[02.01]] Mathematics is the domain's core, the general science of quantity, structure, space, and change; [[02.03]] Logic isolates the laws of valid inference on which mathematical proof itself depends; [[02.02]] Computer Science studies computation — what can be computed, how efficiently, and by what algorithms and machines; [[02.04]] Information Theory quantifies information, compression, and the limits of communication over noisy channels; and [[02.05]] Systems Theory studies organization, feedback, and emergence in complex systems regardless of their substrate.

The formal sciences supply the languages in which the [[01]] Natural Sciences state their laws and the [[04]] Social Sciences build their models, while computer science and information theory underpin the digital technologies of [[03]] Applied Sciences & Technology and the practices of [[11]] Digital Preservation. See [Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Philosophy of Mathematics](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/philosophy-mathematics/).

records.name: Applied Sciences & Technology
records.en: The systematic application of scientific knowledge to practical human ends — building, healing, feeding, powering, connecting, and making. Spans engineering, medicine, agriculture, architecture, manufacturing, transportation, energy, telecommunications, biotechnology, and nanotechnology; distinguished from the natural sciences by its criterion of usefulness rather than truth.
records.cs: Soustavné uplatňování vědeckých poznatků k praktickým lidským cílům — stavět, léčit, živit, pohánět, spojovat a vyrábět. Zahrnuje inženýrství, lékařství, zemědělství, architekturu, výrobu, dopravu, energetiku, telekomunikace, biotechnologie a nanotechnologie; od přírodních věd se liší kritériem užitečnosti, nikoli pravdivosti.
records.brief:
Applied sciences and technology turn scientific understanding into working systems that serve human needs — shelter, health, food, movement, power, and communication. Where the natural sciences ask whether a claim is true, the applied sciences ask whether a design works: their results are judged by reliability, efficiency, safety, and cost under real constraints, and their history is the history of civilization's expanding material capability.

[[03.01]] Engineering is the domain's methodological core, the disciplined design of structures, machines, and systems; [[03.02]] Medicine applies biological science to preventing and treating disease; [[03.03]] Agriculture applies it to producing food and fiber; [[03.04]] Architecture unites engineering with design in the built environment; [[03.05]] Manufacturing converts materials into finished goods at scale; [[03.06]] Transportation and [[03.08]] Telecommunications move people, goods, and information; [[03.07]] Energy captures, converts, and distributes power; and [[03.09]] Biotechnology and [[03.10]] Nanotechnology engineer living systems and matter at the molecular scale.

The domain draws its principles from the [[01]] Natural Sciences and its computational methods from the [[02]] Formal Sciences, while [[07]] Practical Skills & Trades carry out its designs in the field and [[12]] Post-Disaster Rebuilding distills its essentials into a bootstrap kit for reconstruction. See [Encyclopaedia Britannica: technology](https://www.britannica.com/technology/technology).

records.name: Social Sciences
records.en: The empirical study of human behavior, societies, and institutions — how individuals think and act, how groups organize, exchange, govern, and learn. Spans psychology, sociology, anthropology, economics, political science, law, education, geography, demography, and archaeology; distinguished from the humanities by its reliance on systematic observation and measurement.
records.cs: Empirické studium lidského chování, společností a institucí — toho, jak jednotlivci myslí a jednají a jak se společnosti organizují, hospodaří, vládnou a vzdělávají. Zahrnuje psychologii, sociologii, antropologii, ekonomii, politologii, právo, pedagogiku, geografii, demografii a archeologii; od humanitních věd se liší důrazem na systematické pozorování a měření.
records.brief:
The social sciences study human beings in their individual and collective life — how people think, decide, and develop; how societies organize, produce, and govern; and how populations distribute themselves across space and time. Their defining commitment is to investigate human affairs with systematic observation, comparison, and measurement, turning surveys, experiments, statistics, fieldwork, and excavation on subject matter that the humanities approach through interpretation.

[[04.01]] Psychology examines mind and behavior in the individual; [[04.02]] Sociology and [[04.03]] Anthropology study societies and cultures, the one chiefly in complex modern settings, the other comparatively across all of humanity; [[04.04]] Economics analyzes production, exchange, and allocation under scarcity; [[04.05]] Political Science and [[04.06]] Law treat power, governance, and binding rules; [[04.07]] Education studies teaching and learning; [[04.08]] Geography and [[04.09]] Demography map human activity and population structure; and [[04.10]] Archaeology recovers past societies from their material remains.

The domain borrows experimental and statistical method from the [[01]] Natural Sciences and formal modeling from the [[02]] Formal Sciences, while sharing its subject — humanity — with the [[05]] Humanities, which study meaning and culture through interpretive rather than quantitative means. See [Encyclopaedia Britannica: social science](https://www.britannica.com/topic/social-science).

records.name: Humanities
records.en: The interpretive study of human culture and meaning — the record of what people have thought, written, believed, and made of themselves. Spans history, philosophy, linguistics, literature, and the study of religion, culture, media, gender, ethnicity, and the classical world; distinguished from the social sciences by interpretation, criticism, and close reading rather than measurement.
records.cs: Interpretativní studium lidské kultury a významu — záznamu toho, co lidé mysleli, čemu věřili, co psali a čím se stali. Zahrnuje historii, filozofii, lingvistiku, literaturu a studium náboženství, kultury, médií, genderu, etnicity a antického světa; od společenských věd se liší interpretací, kritikou a pozorným čtením namísto měření.
records.brief:
The humanities study human culture and meaning — what people have thought, believed, written, said, and valued — through interpretation, criticism, and close engagement with texts, languages, and traditions. Their aim is understanding rather than prediction: a humanistic account succeeds when it renders a work, an era, or a practice intelligible in its own terms and in ours.

[[05.01]] History reconstructs and interprets the human past from its sources; [[05.02]] Philosophy examines the most general questions of knowledge, reality, and value; [[05.03]] Linguistics analyzes the structure of human language; [[05.04]] Literature studies verbal art and its traditions; [[05.05]] Religious Studies treats belief systems and their practices comparatively; [[05.07]] Classics unites language, literature, and history in the study of the ancient Mediterranean world; and [[05.06]] Cultural Studies, [[05.08]] Media Studies, [[05.09]] Gender Studies, and [[05.10]] Ethnic Studies bring critical interpretation to contemporary culture, communication, and identity.

The humanities share their subject with the [[04]] Social Sciences but differ in method — interpretation and argument rather than measurement. They analyze the works whose creation belongs to [[06]] Arts & Creative Expression and whose living transmission is the concern of [[10]] Cultural Preservation. See [Encyclopaedia Britannica: humanities](https://www.britannica.com/topic/humanities) and the [Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy](https://plato.stanford.edu/).

records.name: Arts & Creative Expression
records.en: The creation of works valued for aesthetic, expressive, and communicative power — image, performance, designed object, crafted artifact, and cuisine. Spans the visual and performing arts, design, crafts, and the culinary arts; distinguished from the humanities, which study and interpret such works, by its focus on the practice of making them.
records.cs: Tvorba děl ceněných pro estetickou, výrazovou a sdělnou sílu — obraz, představení, navržený předmět, řemeslný artefakt i pokrm. Zahrnuje výtvarná umění, scénická umění, design, umělecká řemesla a kulinářské umění; od humanitních věd, jež taková díla studují a vykládají, se liší zaměřením na samotnou praxi tvorby.
records.brief:
Arts and creative expression comprise the making of works valued for their aesthetic, expressive, and communicative power — images, performances, designed objects, crafted artifacts, and food raised to an art. The domain is defined by practice: its knowledge lives in technique, composition, and judgment exercised in the act of creation, and its works answer to standards of beauty, originality, and effect rather than of truth or utility alone.

[[06.01]] Visual Arts encompass painting, sculpture, drawing, photography, and their kin — works made primarily to be seen; [[06.02]] Performing Arts — music, theatre, dance, and performed film — unfold in time before an audience; [[06.03]] Design applies aesthetic judgment to functional objects, environments, and communication; [[06.04]] Crafts carry the traditions of skilled handwork in ceramics, textiles, glass, wood, and metal; and [[06.05]] Culinary Arts treat the preparation of food as a compositional practice.

The domain's works are studied and interpreted by the [[05]] Humanities, its functional side shades into the trades of [[07]] Practical Skills & Trades, and its inherited techniques and repertoires are safeguarded by [[10]] Cultural Preservation. See [Encyclopaedia Britannica: the arts](https://www.britannica.com/topic/the-arts).

records.name: Practical Skills & Trades
records.en: Hands-on skills and trades that build, maintain, and repair the physical fabric of daily life — structures, machines, circuits, pipes, wood, metal, gardens, food, and cloth. Spans construction, mechanics, electronics, plumbing, carpentry, welding, gardening, cooking, sewing, and automotive work; distinguished from engineering by its basis in manual craft and working practice over design theory.
records.cs: Praktické dovednosti a řemesla, jež budují, udržují a opravují hmotné zázemí každodenního života — stavby, stroje, obvody, potrubí, dřevo, kov, zahrady, jídlo i textil. Zahrnují stavebnictví, mechaniku, elektroniku, instalatérství, tesařství, svařování, zahradničení, vaření, šití a automechaniku; od inženýrství se liší tím, že vycházejí z ruční zručnosti a pracovní praxe, nikoli z teorie návrhu.
records.brief:
Practical skills and trades are the hands-on disciplines that build, maintain, and repair the physical fabric of daily life. Their knowledge is embodied and procedural — acquired through apprenticeship and practice, verified by whether the joint holds, the circuit carries, and the engine runs — and it forms the working counterpart to the design knowledge of engineering.

[[07.01]] Construction erects and finishes buildings; [[07.05]] Carpentry and [[07.06]] Welding work wood and metal into structure; [[07.02]] Mechanics and [[07.10]] Automotive keep machines and vehicles running; [[07.03]] Electronics assembles and repairs circuits and devices; [[07.04]] Plumbing installs and maintains water and waste systems; and [[07.07]] Gardening, [[07.08]] Cooking, and [[07.09]] Sewing sustain the household economy of food and clothing.

The trades execute and maintain what [[03]] Applied Sciences & Technology designs, shade into [[06]] Arts & Creative Expression where craft rises to aesthetic ambition, and supply the manual competence on which [[08]] Survival & Emergency Preparedness and [[12]] Post-Disaster Rebuilding depend when specialized infrastructure is unavailable.

records.name: Survival & Emergency Preparedness
records.en: Knowledge that sustains life when normal infrastructure fails — treating injury, securing water, food, shelter, fire, and warmth, finding one's way, communicating, staying safe, and keeping a clear mind. Spans first aid, water purification, food preservation, shelter, fire making, navigation, emergency communication, defense, disaster response, and psychological resilience.
records.cs: Znalosti, jež udržují život při selhání běžné infrastruktury — ošetření zranění, zajištění vody, potravy, přístřeší, ohně a tepla, orientace v terénu, komunikace, obrana a zachování jasné mysli. Zahrnují první pomoc, úpravu vody, konzervaci potravin, stavbu přístřeší, rozdělávání ohně, navigaci, nouzovou komunikaci, obranu a bezpečnost, reakci na katastrofy a psychickou odolnost.
records.brief:
Survival and emergency preparedness comprise the knowledge that sustains human life when normal infrastructure fails — in wilderness, disaster, or societal disruption. The domain is organized by the hierarchy of survival needs: immediate medical care, then water, shelter, fire, and food, then the capacities to navigate, communicate, stay secure, and endure. Its standard of value is stark — knowledge earns its place by keeping people alive with minimal tools and time.

[[08.01]] First Aid & Medical stabilizes injury and illness without a hospital; [[08.02]] Water Procurement & Purification and [[08.03]] Food Preservation & Storage secure the two consumables life depends on; [[08.04]] Shelter Construction and [[08.05]] Fire Making protect the body's core temperature; [[08.06]] Navigation and [[08.07]] Emergency Communication restore orientation and contact; [[08.08]] Defense & Security and [[08.09]] Disaster Response address threat and large-scale crisis; and [[08.10]] Psychological Resilience maintains the judgment on which every other skill depends.

The domain condenses the medicine, chemistry, and engineering of the [[01]] Natural Sciences and [[03]] Applied Sciences & Technology into field-usable procedure, draws manual competence from [[07]] Practical Skills & Trades, and hands off to [[12]] Post-Disaster Rebuilding once immediate survival is secured and reconstruction begins.

records.name: Reference & Documentation
records.en: Compiled works organized for consultation rather than continuous reading — the codified record of facts, terms, methods, places, and designs. Spans encyclopedias, dictionaries, technical manuals, maps and atlases, standards, formulas and tables, protocols, blueprints, patents, and historical archives; its value rests on accuracy, organization, and retrievability.
records.cs: Souborná díla uspořádaná k vyhledávání, nikoli k souvislé četbě — kodifikovaný záznam faktů, pojmů, postupů, míst a návrhů. Zahrnují encyklopedie, slovníky, technické příručky, mapy a atlasy, normy a specifikace, vzorce a tabulky, protokoly a postupy, výkresy a schémata, patenty a historické archivy; jejich hodnota spočívá v přesnosti, uspořádání a dohledatelnosti.
records.brief:
Reference and documentation comprise compiled works organized for consultation rather than continuous reading — the codified record of facts, terms, methods, places, designs, and precedents. The domain's genres share a common architecture: authoritative content, systematic arrangement, and retrieval apparatus — indexes, keys, coordinates, numbering — that lets a reader extract one fact from millions. Its cardinal virtues are accuracy, currency, and retrievability.

[[09.01]] Encyclopedias survey knowledge at large and [[09.02]] Dictionaries codify the words that carry it; [[09.03]] Technical Manuals and [[09.07]] Protocols & Procedures prescribe how to operate, maintain, and act; [[09.04]] Maps & Atlases fix knowledge to place; [[09.05]] Standards & Specifications and [[09.06]] Formulas & Tables state the agreed measures and constants on which engineering and science rely; [[09.08]] Blueprints & Schematics and [[09.09]] Patents record designs and inventions; and [[09.10]] Historical Archives preserve the primary documents from which history is written.

Every other domain deposits its distilled knowledge here, which makes the reference shelf the natural payload of preservation: [[11]] Digital Preservation keeps its digital forms intact, while the [[05]] Humanities and [[10]] Cultural Preservation depend on its archives for sources and memory. See [Encyclopaedia Britannica: reference work](https://www.britannica.com/topic/reference-work).

records.name: Cultural Preservation
records.en: The safeguarding of intangible human heritage — the languages, stories, songs, customs, recipes, games, and rituals through which communities transmit identity across generations. Spans folklore and mythology, traditions, music, narratives, traditional art techniques, and oral histories; it keeps cultural practice alive, where the humanities analyze it.
records.cs: Ochrana nehmotného lidského dědictví — jazyků, příběhů, písní, zvyků, receptů, her a rituálů, jimiž společenství předávají identitu z generace na generaci. Zahrnuje folklor a mytologii, tradice, hudbu, vyprávění, tradiční umělecké techniky a orální historii; udržuje kulturní praxi živou, zatímco humanitní vědy ji analyzují.
records.brief:
Cultural preservation safeguards intangible human heritage — the languages, stories, songs, customs, recipes, games, rituals, and techniques through which communities transmit identity from generation to generation. Its subject is living practice: knowledge that exists chiefly in memory, speech, and performance, and that disappears when transmission breaks. The domain therefore combines documentation — recording, transcription, archiving — with revitalization, keeping practices in active use.

[[10.01]] Languages preserves linguistic diversity, the medium of all the rest; [[10.02]] Folklore & Mythology and [[10.06]] Stories & Narratives keep the inherited tale-worlds of communities; [[10.05]] Music & Songs and [[10.09]] Traditional Art Techniques carry performed and made tradition; [[10.03]] Traditions & Customs, [[10.08]] Rituals & Ceremonies, and [[10.07]] Games & Recreation preserve patterned social practice; [[10.04]] Traditional Recipes keeps foodways; and [[10.10]] Oral Histories records first-person testimony before it is lost.

Where the [[05]] Humanities analyze culture and [[06]] Arts & Creative Expression creates it, cultural preservation keeps it transmissible; its recordings and transcripts join the archives of [[09]] Reference & Documentation, and their digital forms depend on [[11]] Digital Preservation. See [UNESCO: What is Intangible Cultural Heritage?](https://ich.unesco.org/en/what-is-intangible-heritage-00003).

records.name: Digital Preservation
records.en: Techniques for keeping digital information intact, readable, and secure over time — encoding it in durable formats, compressing it efficiently, protecting it cryptographically, replicating it in backups, and recovering it after loss. Spans file formats, compression, encryption and security, backup strategies, and data recovery; it underwrites every digitally stored domain.
records.cs: Postupy, jež uchovávají digitální informace neporušené, čitelné a zabezpečené v čase — kódování do trvanlivých formátů, účinná komprese, kryptografická ochrana, replikace v zálohách a obnova po ztrátě. Zahrnují souborové formáty, kompresi, šifrování a bezpečnost, zálohovací strategie a obnovu dat; podpírají každou digitálně uloženou oblast.
records.brief:
Digital preservation comprises the techniques that keep digital information intact, readable, and secure across time and technological change. Digital data faces distinctive threats — media decay, format obsolescence, silent corruption, and unauthorized access — and the domain answers each with engineering discipline: durable encodings, redundancy, integrity checking, and planned migration. Its horizon is measured in decades, against hardware and software generations measured in years.

[[11.01]] File Formats determine whether stored information remains interpretable — open, documented formats are preservation's foundation; [[11.02]] Compression Methods trade storage for computation within limits set by information theory; [[11.03]] Encryption & Security protects integrity and confidentiality; [[11.04]] Backup Strategies multiply copies across media, locations, and time; and [[11.05]] Data Recovery salvages information after failure, corruption, or loss.

The domain applies the computer science and information theory of the [[02]] Formal Sciences to a custodial mission it shares with analog archiving: it carries the reference corpus of [[09]] Reference & Documentation and the recordings of [[10]] Cultural Preservation forward through time. See [Digital Preservation Coalition: Digital Preservation Handbook](https://www.dpconline.org/handbook).

records.name: Post-Disaster Rebuilding
records.en: Knowledge for reconstructing the material and social foundations of civilization from minimal means — restoring water, sanitation, and power, making tools, producing essential chemicals and medicines, and organizing communities. Spans basic infrastructure, tool making, essential chemistry, basic medicine production, and community organization; it begins where immediate survival ends.
records.cs: Znalosti pro obnovu hmotných a společenských základů civilizace z minimálních prostředků — obnovení vody, hygieny a energie, výroba nástrojů, příprava nezbytných chemikálií a léčiv a organizace společenství. Zahrnují základní infrastrukturu, výrobu nástrojů, nezbytnou chemii, výrobu základních léčiv a organizaci komunity; začínají tam, kde končí bezprostřední přežití.
records.brief:
Post-disaster rebuilding comprises the knowledge needed to reconstruct the material and social foundations of civilization from minimal means — after war, pandemic, natural catastrophe, or systemic collapse. The domain is a deliberate compression of civilization's technical inheritance: for each essential capability it asks what must be known to recreate it from scratch, without supply chains, specialists, or intact institutions.

[[12.01]] Basic Infrastructure restores water supply, sanitation, power, and roads — the substrate every other recovery depends on; [[12.02]] Tool Making bootstraps the instruments of production, from forge to machine tools; [[12.03]] Essential Chemistry recreates the key substances — soap, lime, acids, fertilizers, fuels — on which health and industry rest; [[12.04]] Basic Medicine Production restores antiseptics, analgesics, and antibiotics; and [[12.05]] Community Organization rebuilds the cooperation, order, and decision-making that make collective work possible.

The domain begins where [[08]] Survival & Emergency Preparedness ends — when the crisis is survived and reconstruction starts — and it distills the [[01]] Natural Sciences and [[03]] Applied Sciences & Technology into a bootstrap sequence executed with the manual skills of [[07]] Practical Skills & Trades, guided by the preserved record of [[09]] Reference & Documentation. See [The Knowledge (Lewis Dartnell)](https://the-knowledge.org/).
